Shell(cd /Users/rezuan/Rezuan/projects/commandcode-test-project && git commit -F - <<'EOF' Real authentication with a TOTP second factor Phase 1 of the gap-closure plan. Until now the acting role came from an X-Demo-Role request header that any caller could set, so anyone could be an administrator by typing one line. The permission matrix was enforced correctly but the identity behind it was fiction, and a second factor cannot be built on fiction. Sign-in is now real: bcrypt-hashed passwords, signed JWT sessions, and TOTP with single-use recovery codes. The flow is deliberately two-step. A password alone yields a short-lived challenge token that can only be exchanged for a code; only the code step issues a session. So a stolen password is not by itself enough, and a challenge token cannot be replayed as a session. Both are covered by tests, along with a wrong password, a wrong code, a reused recovery code, and disabling 2FA without the password. The permission matrix itself is unchanged. RequirePermission and RequireAdmin now read the role from the token instead of a header, so all the existing enforcement and its tests carry over intact. A schema upgrade path, because this caused a real failure. The deployed Neon database already held data, and create_all() never alters an existing table, so adding the password and 2FA columns would have produced a missing-column error at request time. sync_schema() adds missing tables and columns at startup. It is additive only, and raises rather than guessing a value for a NOT NULL column with no server default. Applied to Neon: six columns and one table added, 89 accounts and 5 users preserved. Alembic remains the right long-term answer and is noted as such in DEPLOYMENT.md. That upgrade also revealed a second problem: users seeded before passwords existed had none, so nobody could have signed in. ensure_demo_users() repairs such accounts on boot and, importantly, never overwrites a password that has already been set. Interface: a sign-in screen listing the demo accounts, a two-step code prompt, a Security page for enrolling 2FA and changing your password, and the old role switcher replaced by the signed-in user with a sign-out button. A 401 now returns to sign-in and clears the dead token; sign-in calls opt out of that, since a wrong password is also a 401. Demo reset is now Admin-only: it deletes every posted transaction, and it was previously open to anyone signed in. Verified against the live Neon database, not just locally: signed in as Admin, read the workbook figures through real auth, 401 without a token and 200 with one. 87 backend tests pass on both SQLite and Postgres, up from 59. 20 frontend tests pass.
